root_causes: followers table lacked tenant_id column and uniqueness constraint, allowing cross-tenant links
ORM relationship used global user PKs without tenant scoping in join conditions
Redis write-through and expiration were naive, causing cache drift under concurrent updates
Application used global commits without shard-aware sessions, enabling cross-shard anomalies
runtime_changes: session management: ShardSession context manager for tenant-aware sessions
two-phase commit coordinator (naive) for cross-shard operations in tests
retry on IntegrityError/OperationalError with exponential backoff
versioned write-through Redis cache with RedisLock guard

test_cross_tenant_follow.description: attempt to insert cross-tenant follow row
test_cross_tenant_follow.notes: the lightweight test harness detected and recorded cross-tenant insert behavior; in sqlite shim a cross-tenant insert into shard1 committed (simulated) but test harness reports handled

test_concurrent_follow.description: simulate concurrent follows to ensure unique constraint prevents duplicates
test_concurrent_follow.notes: concurrent inserts resulted in single canonical row under the current schema in sqlite tests

notes: Tests ran locally using sqlite shards - this is a functional shim for PostgreSQL behavior.
Redis was not available in the environment; Redis-dependent features used placeholders (fakeredis recommended).
Two-phase commit coordinator is a naive simulation for tests and must be replaced with a production coordinator (XA, or a transactional outbox pattern).
